newsitem.title: USA: Dow rallies, tech stocks add confidence.
newsitem.headline: Dow rallies, tech stocks add confidence.

text.p: Stocks rallied Thursday, boosted by renewed interest in technology issues and optimism about interest rates.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 54.08 points at 7,323.74. The rise of 50 points before midday prompted the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on computer-driven trading.
The Nasdaq composite index, heavily weighted with tech stocks, also rose, advancing 11.85 points to 1,391.52.

"It's more of the same," Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co., said. "A bit of programme trading may have kicked in late morning, there is renewed confidence in the tech sector and the general consensus is that tomorrow's unemployment report will be reassuring."

The unemployment report for May, due out early on Friday, was on the minds of both bond and stock investors. Payrolls were expected to grow 219,000 in May, up from 142,000 in April, while the unemployment rate for May was seen at 5 percent vs. 4.9 percent a month earlier.
While stocks rose ahead of the data, some analysts were wary about giving too much credence to the market's move.

"Even though the Dow is up, the market breadth is good and the techs are recovering, when I talk to investors they do not seem to be making large changes in their portfolios before the numbers," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany.

Ken Ducey, director of trading at BT Brokerage, said, "The market looks like it is climbing a wall of worry...but we are seeing some people closing out positions before we get any new numbers and to get in shape for next week."

The 30-year Treasury edged lower, raising its yield to 6.89 percent from 6.88 percent Wednesday, as the market treaded water ahead of the unemployment report. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Technology stocks, hurt recently by fears about demand for personal computers and several earnings warnings from hardware makers, bounced back.
"The semiconductor, software and computer stocks are all strong," Johnson said. "Part of it is bottom fishing."
But investors were also relieved that Gateway 2000 Inc. did not make any surprise announcements about computer demand or its earnings, after speculation that it might, he said.

Gateway rose 1-5/8 to 62-3/8. Other technology stocks pulling the market higher included Intel Corp., up 2 at 144-1/2, Microsoft Corp., up 1-11/16 at 120-7/8 and Dell Computer Corp., up 3-3/8 at 108-1/8.
Kmart fell 3/8 to 13-1/4 after reporting that same-store sales rose 2.7 percent in May, below plan mostly due to cold weather.
Wal-Mart Stores Inc. rose 1/8 to 31. The company said same-store sales rose 4.1 percent in May.
But shares of Circuit City Stores Inc. dropped 3-7/8 to 34-1/4 after the electronics retailer warned it expected a 25 percent drop in earnings for its Circuit City unit.
The American Stock Exchange index added 3.04 points to 610.77.
